families.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
families.definition: Methods that retrieve relevant external information from heterogeneous sources or knowledge bases to condition response generation.

properties.text: These systems retrieve relevant information from heterogeneous knowledge sources to homogenize them for dialogue generation.
They leverage internet search or large corpora to access continually updating knowledge that is not frozen in model weights.
Retrieval-based approaches often use a generate-and-rank strategy to fetch a batch of response candidates from various neural models.
Some methods use on-demand machine reading to perform QA-style comprehension on retrieved long-form text.
This approach helps alleviate factual inaccuracies and hallucinations by grounding responses in retrieved evidence.

limitations.text: Retrieval-based models face the challenge of simultaneously reasoning to provide correct knowledge and generating conversation.
Retrieved background knowledge in open settings is often noisy, resulting in severe challenges in information transmission.
Existing methods often suffer from inference efficiency issues due to the explicit retrieval process.
The precision of knowledge retrieval can be low, and entities may not be included in the knowledge base.
Using all retrieved knowledge may introduce noise, while selecting only one may lose valuable information.

families.name: Knowledge-Integrated Pre-trained Models
families.definition: Architectures that inject domain-specific knowledge directly into pre-trained language model parameters or adapters to bypass explicit retrieval.

properties.text: These models use lightweight adapters to inject knowledge into pre-trained language models, bypassing explicit retrieval.
Knowledge bases can be embedded directly into model parameters to handle KBs of any size without scaling issues.
Some methods use knowledge-injected pre-trained language models for both natural language understanding and generation tasks.
This approach allows for end-to-end training where the model learns to utilize knowledge without separate retrieval modules.

limitations.text: Pre-trained models often lack explicit awareness of domain-specific knowledge essential for downstream tasks.
Performance drops dramatically when the input contains entities that do not appear in pre-training and fine-tuning datasets.
These models may still hallucinate facts if the knowledge is not sufficiently integrated or if the context is ambiguous.

families.name: Modular and Pipeline Systems
families.definition: Systems that decompose dialogue generation into distinct stages such as knowledge selection, reasoning, and response generation.

properties.text: Modular models break down the problem into easier steps, such as first generating a knowledge sequence and then the response.
Pipelined approaches handle knowledge-seeking turn detection, knowledge selection, and response generation in sequence.
These systems can integrate traditional modular approaches to incorporate domain knowledge with modern deep learning techniques.
Modular generation allows for better control over the reasoning process before the final response is produced.

limitations.text: Pipeline systems often use hard-label decisions to activate subtasks, which can hinder model performance.
Modularized systems rely on dialogue state tracking to interact with knowledge bases, which is expensive in terms of annotation and inference time.
Independent or pipeline systems may fail to capture the bilateral information flow between personal knowledge and conversation.

families.name: Knowledge Graph Grounding
families.definition: Methods that utilize the structural information of knowledge graphs to guide response generation and ensure factual consistency.

properties.text: These systems integrate knowledge graphs into the response generation process by training models to answer using KG elements.
Some approaches use attention-based walks over knowledge graphs to introduce engaging and contextually diverse entities.
Knowledge graph aware decoding can be used with pre-trained transformers to generate knowledge-grounded responses.
Dynamic knowledge graph embeddings can evolve as the dialogue progresses to model structured knowledge.

limitations.text: Integrating knowledge graphs into the dialogue generation process in an end-to-end manner is a non-trivial task.
Models may generate factually incorrect statements if they do not strictly adhere to the known facts supplied by the KG.
The generation of well-grounded responses requires careful handling of the graph structure to avoid inconsistencies.

families.name: Document-Grounded Dialogue
families.definition: Systems that ground conversations in specific long-form documents, requiring the identification and utilization of relevant passages.

properties.text: These systems identify relevant knowledge in conversational systems grounded in long documents by leveraging document structure.
Models use dialogue-contextualized passage encodings to better locate knowledge relevant to the conversation.
Document-grounded datasets provide a source of information that models can use to generate more informative responses.
Some methods jointly denoise the dialogue context and aggregate document information for response generation.

limitations.text: Dialogue history that is not related to the current dialogue may introduce noise in the knowledge selection processing.
Identifying relevant knowledge in long documents is critical but challenging for effective response generation.
Existing studies often assume the rule text is provided, neglecting the essential retrieval step in real scenarios.

families.name: Task-Oriented Knowledge Integration
families.definition: Approaches for task-oriented dialogue that incorporate external knowledge to handle requests beyond the scope of domain APIs.

properties.text: These systems expand coverage by incorporating external unstructured knowledge sources for out-of-API-coverage queries.
Methods use schema-guided knowledge decision and negatives-enhanced knowledge selection to boost response quality.
Some approaches use template-guided hybrid pointer networks to retrieve potentially relevant answers from domain-specific repositories.
Entity-aware knowledge retrieval and copy mechanisms are used to generate responses for task-oriented dialogue systems.

limitations.text: Most prior work is restricted to limited coverage of domain APIs, leaving many user requests unaddressed.
End-to-end systems using knowledge bases directly cannot scale when the KB is larger than a few hundred entries.
The precision of knowledge retrieval and the inclusion of entities in the knowledge base remain practical challenges.

families.name: Low-Resource and Zero-Resource Learning
families.definition: Techniques designed to build knowledge-grounded dialogue systems with limited or no context-knowledge-response training triples.

properties.text: These methods use weakly supervised learning frameworks that benefit from large-scale ungrounded dialogue data.
Zero-resource settings assume no context-knowledge-response triples are needed for training.
Disentangled response decoders isolate parameters that depend on knowledge-grounded dialogues from the entire generation model.
Three-stage learning frameworks are used to address the laborious construction of knowledge-grounded dialogues.

limitations.text: Existing models usually perform poorly when transferred to new domains with limited training samples.
Learning such a model often requires knowledge-grounded dialogues that are difficult to obtain.
The lack of training data and heterogeneous knowledge sources makes these systems challenging to build.

families.name: Emotional and Empathetic Dialogue
families.definition: Models that incorporate emotional perception and expression to generate empathetic and human-like responses.

properties.text: These systems integrate multi-source information including emotion flow, facial expressions, and speaker personalities.
Generated sentences are designed to be emotive and empathetic, similar to how a doctor communicates.
Models use internal and external memory to generate responses that are emotionally consistent.
Datasets like EmpatheticDialogues provide conversations grounded in emotional situations to facilitate training.

limitations.text: The paucity of suitable publicly-available datasets for training and evaluation is a significant challenge.
Multiple types of emotional information are often insufficiently exploited in emotional conversation fields.
Recognizing feelings in the conversation partner and replying accordingly is a significant challenge for AI systems.

families.name: Response Selection and Matching
families.definition: Retrieval-based methods that select the most appropriate response from a set of candidates based on context matching.

properties.text: These systems predict an appropriate response given a dialogue context by matching context and response representations.
Speaker-aware models account for speaker change information, which is an intrinsic property of multi-turn dialogues.
Source-aware networks distinguish between different information sources such as user utterances and knowledge base results.
Sequential match networks match responses with each utterance on multiple granularities to distill important matching information.

limitations.text: Existing works often ignore relationships among utterances or miss important information in the context.
Obtaining key information from a complex, long dialogue context is challenging, especially with multiple information sources.
Retrieval-based models may lack the fluency and informativeness of generative models in some contexts.
Building knowledge-grounded dialogue systems is challenging due to the lack of training data and heterogeneous knowledge sources.
Existing systems perform poorly on unseen topics due to limited topics covered in the training data.
It is challenging to generalize to domains that require different types of knowledge sources.
Large language models often hallucinate factual inaccuracies, impeding their widespread adoption.
There is a need for methods that can both reason to provide correct knowledge and generate conversation simultaneously.
The precision of knowledge retrieval and the handling of entities not included in the knowledge base remain unresolved.
Integrating knowledge graphs into the dialogue generation process in an end-to-end manner is non-trivial.
There is a lack of large-scale, publicly available datasets for training and evaluating empathetic and emotional dialogue.
Most prior work on task-oriented dialogue systems is restricted to limited coverage of domain APIs.
End-to-end systems using knowledge bases directly cannot scale when the knowledge base is large.
There is a need for metrics that go beyond single-word metrics like perplexity to measure performance across sequences of utterances.
The problem of building a coherent and non-monotonous conversational agent with proper discourse and coverage remains open.
